title: Compare localized formats without corrupting data
goal: Use prepared de_DE.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8 for numeric/time categories, inspect monetary locale metadata and explicit C sorting.
challenge: Choose display categories and machine-processing locale independently for a supplied small dataset. Retain actual outputs/statuses and preserve originals; report reasoning through self-review, not a score.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/foundation-locale-formats.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && umask 077; here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/foundation-locale-formats.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700; }; fresh() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test ! -e "$1" && test ! -L "$1"; }; regular() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h "$1")" = learner:600:1; }; here && test "$(df -B1 --output=avail / | tail -1)" -ge 1073741824 && pwd
steps.explanation: Record this unique guest-only workspace. On Resume re-establish the recorded path/definitions; never overwrite another exercise.
steps.expected: Private learner-owned700 directory and observed1GiB free admission.

steps.command: here && locale -a && env LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 locale -k decimal_point thousands_sep currency_symbol && env LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 locale -k decimal_point currency_symbol && env LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 date -d "2026-01-01 UTC" +%A && env LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 date -d "2026-01-01 UTC" +%A
steps.explanation: Inspect actual categories and a fixed instant rather than locale assumptions. Monetary metadata is inspected, not a money arithmetic exercise.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/source.txt" && printf "z\n\303\244\n" > source.txt && fresh "$w/source.sha" && sha256sum source.txt > source.sha && fresh "$w/c.txt" && fresh "$w/de.txt" && env LC_ALL=C sort source.txt > c.txt && env LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 sort source.txt > de.txt && cat c.txt de.txt && sha256sum -c source.sha
steps.explanation: Keep original UTF-8 bytes. A machine-processing locale should be explicit; collation depends on dataset and locale implementation.
steps.expected: Actual C versus German ordering retained without rewriting source.

hints: Do not assume a localized decimal comma is a TSV separator or that every locale orders every sample differently.
Choose command scope deliberately; compare known bytes and actual statuses, not only a successful-looking display.
Retain before evidence; refuse collisions and restore exact policy state before leaving. Guest root can bypass guest-side guards.
review: I demonstrated the selected mode’s actual observations and retained an incorrect or incomplete case.
I preserved originals and can explain the reasoning and limitations; this records self-review, not automatic assessment.
I restored any changed default/zone and retained the exact workspace without touching unrelated files.
coverage: LPIC-1 active v5.0 partial 107.3 non-English localization and LC_*; 103.2 sorting: reinforcement. No complete-objective coverage or endorsement.
